answer: Neighborhood persistence scoring: weight each agent's influence by how long its transaction partners keep interacting with it after first contact. A fresh node's edges decay unless neighbors return, forming a durable marble of repeated exchange around established agents. An attacker mass-creating identities gets no such history, so each fake agent must sustain real reciprocal activity across many rounds—a fable of patience, not a quick spawn.
